    Vectorize strpm_simd hot paths using std::experimental::simd
    
    Four targeted optimizations, all pure std::experimental::simd (no intrinsics):
    
    A. simd_popcount8 helper (strpm_simd.hpp): bit-parallel Hamming-weight
       over all 8 uint8 lanes in 5 SIMD operations, replacing 8 scalar
       std::popcount calls.
    
    B. prog_tmp – vectorize nlb_counts, eliminate nlb_before lambda:
       simd_popcount8 computes all per-string NLB contributions at once;
       the prefix-sum loop now does additions only.  nlb_before is derived
       as nlb_counts - per_elem (mathematical identity for inclusive prefix
       sums), removing the element-wise lambda entirely.
    
    C. prog_tmp – replace after_match/before_levels lambdas with direct
       mask arithmetic: a static lane_indices constant [0..7] is compared
       against match and lvls.size() to produce masks directly, avoiding
       intermediate simd_uint8 temporaries that were immediately thresholded.
    
    D. compare – CSE + bit-isolation trick + shift:
       - Factor out tmp_masks ^ best_masks into `diff`; use `diff << 1`
         instead of `diff * 2`.
       - Hoist `combined = shorter_string + first_length_difference` and
         `relevant_xor = bit_xor & combined` (each computed 4× before).
       - Replace the per-lane countr_zero+shift lambda for first_bit_difference
         with the two's-complement trick x & (0 - x), isolating the lowest
         set bit across all lanes in 2 SIMD ops.
    
    All 224 test games pass (strpm-simd solver).
    
    https://claude.ai/code/session_01FhtQpfWLDw9qZLcxLaYDsr

    Optimize strpm_simd: narrow levels to int16_t, vectorize prog_tmp predicates
    
    Three AVX2-exploiting optimizations using std::experimental::simd only:
    
    1. Narrow level arrays from int (32-bit) to int16_t (16-bit), halving
       cache footprint. All level values fit in [-1, h-2] where h < 32767
       for real games (asserted). Flat arrays (pm_levels, tmp_levels,
       best_levels) gain alignas(16) enabling single-register copy_from/copy_to.
    
    2. Vectorize per-lane stp/afa predicate computation in prog_tmp() using
       simd<int16_t,8> comparisons (<=, ==) and stdx::where masked-assign,
       replacing a scalar loop over active lanes.
    
    3. Vectorize tail-fill of tmp_levels in prog_tmp() using IOTA-based
       simd<int16_t,8> blend with stdx::where, replacing a scalar while-loop.
    
    Benchmarks on 244 hard-benchmarks files (no preprocessing):
    - 221/244 completed within 30s timeout (same for baseline)
    - Total wall time: 202.7s vs 215.6s baseline (~6.3% overall speedup)
    - Average per-file speedup: 1.06x, max: 1.43x on fast files
    
    https://claude.ai/code/session_01TcrZxXbBoxFhc6HKgiNBmP

    strpm_simd: replace SoA vectors with AoS NodePM struct for cache locality
    
    The four separate flat vectors (pm_bits, pm_masks, pm_levels, pm_nlanes)
    were stored in four distinct heap regions, so each to_tmp()/from_tmp()
    call in the lift() hot loop touched up to four independent cache lines.
    
    Replace them with a single std::vector<NodePM> where each 40-byte record
    holds all four fields contiguously:
    
      struct NodePM {
          uint8_t  bits[8];    // offset  0 — SIMD-ready uint8 array
          uint8_t  masks[8];   // offset  8
          int16_t  levels[8];  // offset 16 — SIMD-ready int16 array
          uint8_t  nlanes;     // offset 32
          uint8_t  _pad[7];    // offset 33 — sizeof == 40
      };
    
    With 40 bytes per node, a to_tmp() call now accesses a single contiguous
    memory region (≤2 cache lines) instead of four, cutting cache-miss
    pressure by up to 4× for scattered graph traversals.
    
    All SIMD copy_from/copy_to calls remain compatible because bits[8] and
    masks[8] are still contiguous; memcpy to/from levels[8] has no source-
    alignment constraint.  The initialization loop is simplified to a single
    std::fill(pm.begin(), pm.end(), init).
    
    Benchmark on hard-benchmarks/ (>10ms games, strpm-simd solver):
      38/100 games ≥1.1× faster, 61 neutral, 1 marginally slower.
      Aggregate wall time: 325s → 148s (2.2× speedup).
      Biggest wins: friedmannsubexp_50 18×, pdlbinsudoku7 9.6×,
      pdlbinsudoku8 4.2×, towersofhanoi_10 2.8×.
    
    https://claude.ai/code/session_01RfNC75xb2JQ93tADbzSLGD

    Replace sequential NLB prefix sum with parallel scan using native SIMD intrinsics
    
    The inclusive prefix sum in prog_tmp previously used 7 sequential dependent
    adds. This replaces it with a 3-step parallel scan (log2(8) steps) using
    SSE2 byte-shift + add on x86, NEON vextq + add on ARM, with a fallback to
    the sequential loop for other architectures.

    Vectorize compare() and promote levels to SIMD registers
    
    - Promote tmp_levels/best_levels from scalar uint16_t[8] arrays to
      simd_u16x8 registers, eliminating redundant load/store round-trips
      in to_tmp/from_tmp/to_best/from_best and prog_tmp predicate reload
    - Vectorize compare() level loop: replace 8-iteration scalar loop with
      SIMD predicate masks and find_first_set, reducing branch mispredicts
    - Fix negative pindex bug: clamp to 0 with flag to force both_past when
      pindex < 0, preventing uint16 wrap to 0xFFFF
    - Fix countl_one narrowing: use uint16 countl_one minus 8 instead of
      casting to uint8, staying in native lane width
    - Simplify level arithmetic: remove redundant int↔uint16 double casts
      where uint16 arithmetic suffices

    strpm-simd: guard (k,t) overflow and fall back to tangle learning
    
    The SIMD encoding can only represent a bounded parameter region (bitstrings
    are hard-capped at 8 bits => t <= 7; there are 8 SIMD lanes with nlanes = k-1
    => k <= 9). The (k,t) search previously pushed candidates up to
    floor_log2(nodecount) with no guard, so any sufficiently large game that was
    not solved at small (k,t) would silently overflow the encoding and could
    produce wrong results.
    
    Cap the search at the representable region and, if the game is still unsolved
    once those parameters are exhausted, hand the remaining subgame to a complete
    solver (tangle learning). Because vertices solved by strpm-simd are already in
    the shared oink.disabled bitset (ALWAYS_RESET == 0), TLSolver::run naturally
    operates only on the remainder — no state marshaling needed.
    
    Adds a small Solver::solveRemainderWith(id) helper that constructs and runs
    another registered solver on the same Oink/Game.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>

    strpm: small-buffer-optimize measure storage (no per-node heap)
    
    The scalar solver stored progress measures as vector<vector<bool>> /
    vector<vector<int>> — two heap allocations per node, reached by pointer
    chasing, and copied whole in to_tmp/from_tmp/to_best. Since a measure's length
    is bounded by ~k-1+t (well within 16 for the SIMD-representable range and most
    games), switch bits/levels to boost::container::small_vector with inline
    capacity 16. Common (small) measures now need no heap and the tmp/best/test
    working copies are cheap fixed-size copies; larger measures spill to the heap
    transparently. Bits move from the bit-packed vector<bool> proxy to plain uint8.
    
    Measured on the scalar strpm solver (release, -march=native), cumulative with
    the prior prog_tmp allocation fix:
      TwoCounters10: 13.14s (baseline) -> 10.84s (B1) -> 9.95s (-24% total)
      TwoCounters12: 30.24s (baseline) -> 26.35s (B1) -> 22.84s (-24% total)
    All 224 tests/ games verify; debug build (asserts) clean.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
